speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a pruritic rash on both upper arms; can you describe exactly how the rash looks and when it first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. To narrow this down, have you noticed any seasonal patterns, such as the rash worsening in warmer months or after sun exposure? Also, do you have any other symptoms like joint pain or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Polymorphous Light Eruption (PMLE).

The chronic, pruritic rash on your upper extremities in a young female, combined with your denial of systemic symptoms and lack of new exposures, strongly suggests a sun-induced reaction. Do you have a history of spending significant time outdoors without protection, or does the rash specifically flare up after sun exposure?
